summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on STM32 microcontrollers (I2C driver, ADC, interrupt-driven timers) and a multi-device Linux system on Jetson, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi platforms, with Python and shell scripting. Debugged hardware and firmware issues across UART/I2C buses, resolving 11 integration failures with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1).

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system across a Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller linked by a WebSocket fabric; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Debugged and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++ and drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

Deployed the Jetson-side bridge as a Linux systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation, environment-file config) with static IP networking; configured XRDP for remote administration of the headless Jetson.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands, integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED display.
